query: With whom did this American singer, songwriter and record producer, who contributed to the single "Marvin Gaye" with Julie Frost, co-produced and performed the 2015 song for a movie soundtrack?

pipeline_result.response:
Charlie Puth collaborated with Julie Frost on the single "Marvin Gaye". Charlie Puth is an American singer, songwriter, and record producer known for his work in various genres including hip-hop, pop, and electronic music. He contributed to the 2015 song "Marvin Gaye" by co-writing it along with Meghan Trainor. Additionally, Charlie Puth featured Meghan Trainor on this track as part of a soundtrack performance.

Julie Frost also co-wrote the hook for Black Eyed Peas' "Just Can't Get Enough", Pitbull's "Castle Made of Sand", Flo Rida's "Sweet Spot", Beyoncé's "Countdown", Ed Sheeran's "Kiss Me", Marina and the Diamonds's "Primadonna", Madonna's song "Masterpiece" from her movie soundtrack, and won a Golden Globe award for best original song in a soundtrack.

So, to summarize:
- Charlie Puth contributed to "Marvin Gaye" with Julie Frost.
- Charlie Puth co-wrote the hook for Black Eyed Peas' "Just Can't Get Enough".
- Charlie Puth performed the 2015 song "Marvin Gaye" on a movie soundtrack.
retrieved_context: Marvin Gaye: Marvin Gaye ( ; born Marvin Pentz Gay Jr.; April 2, 1939 – April 1, 1984) was an American singer, songwriter and record producer.  Gaye helped to shape the sound of Motown in the 1960s, first as an in-house session player and later as a solo artist with a string of hits, including "Ain't That Peculiar", "How Sweet It Is (To Be Loved By You)" and "I Heard It Through the Grapevine", and duet recordings with Mary Wells, Kim Weston, Diana Ross and Tammi Terrell, later earning the titles "Prince of Motown" and "Prince of Soul".

Marvin Gaye (song): "Marvin Gaye" is the debut single recorded, produced, and co-written by American singer Charlie Puth.  It was released on February 10, 2015 by Atlantic Records as a single from Puth's third EP, "Some Type of Love" as well as the lead single from his debut album, "Nine Track Mind", it features guest vocals by Meghan Trainor.  Puth co-wrote the song with Julie Frost, Jacob Luttrell and Nick Seeley.

Julie Frost: Julie Frost is an American songwriter, singer, guitar player and music producer.  She is also the founder of the non-profit "Songs For Elephants", with the mission to help mobilize the music and entertainment industry in support of the world's elephants.  She is the second American songwriter to win the Eurovision Song Contest, as co-writer of the song "Satellite", which won the contest for Germany.  Frost wrote the hook for Black Eyed Peas' multi-platinum single "Just Can't Get Enough", the hook for Pitbull's "Castle Made of Sand", and Flo Rida's "Sweet Spot".  She also co-wrote Beyoncé's single "Countdown", Ed Sheeran's "Kiss Me", Marina and the Diamonds's "Primadonna", and Madonna's song "Masterpiece", from the soundtrack of her movie "W.E.", and won a Golden Globe award for best original song in a soundtrack.  Most recently, Frost wrote the end credit song and lead single for the "Endless Love" Soundtrack performed by Tegan and Sara and co-wrote "Lift Me Up" featuring Nico and Vinz and Ladysmith Black Mambazo on Guetta's album "Listen", and co-wrote Charlie Puth's single "Marvin Gaye" with Charlie Puth featuring Meghan Trainor.
